content: PEPAP is an opioid analgesic that is structurally an analogue of pethidine (also known as meperidine). It is chemically related to the compound MPPP, but differs in that it has a phenethyl group replacing the 1-methyl substitution and contains an acetate ester instead of a propionate ester. The pharmacological effects of PEPAP are presumed to be similar to those of other opioids, including the induction of analgesia (pain relief), sedation, and euphoria. However, like other opioids, it is associated with a range of side effects, which may include itching, nausea, and potentially severe respiratory depression. Respiratory depression, in particular, can be life-threatening if not managed appropriately. PEPAP poses additional risks due to its potent inhibition of the enzyme CYP2D6. This property increases the likelihood of adverse drug interactions with other medications metabolized by this enzyme, potentially leading to harmful or unpredictable effects. It remains unclear whether the byproducts formed during the synthesis of PEPAP exhibit neurotoxicity similar to that of MPTP, a known neurotoxic byproduct of MPPP synthesis. Further investigation would be required to determine the neurotoxic potential of PEPAP synthesis byproducts.
